clue.text: A trial for inclusion in the European game

indicators.note: the opening words are to be placed for inclusion inside the following piece, a container signal

parts.note: le is French for 'the', a European language's definite article
a cross is a trial or burden, as in 'a cross to bear'

explanation.surface: Someone is given a trial run to see whether they will make a European sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for inclusion in' puts A CROSS inside LE, the French word for 'the'. LACROSSE is a stick-and-ball team game.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks, so it is an example of a game.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone who has left a job has one pound to their name, free and clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid can mean transparent or limpid, as in liquid eyes or liquid notes, which is the sense of clear.

indicators.note: the compass letter is placed in the old-car word, a container signal

parts.note: a banger is British slang for an old, battered car, as is crate
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep driving east in a clapped-out old car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry on' means to make a fuss; 'banger' is British slang for a rickety old car (also a sausage).
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to make a scene or a fuss, which is what to create means in informal British speech.

indicators.note: away tells us the letter for right is taken out of the defeat word

parts.note: routing an army is bringing it down in heavy defeat

explanation.surface: A trip that brings down the right-wing faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes R from ROUTING to leave OUTING.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is a short pleasure trip or excursion.

clue.text: It's enough to give one the runs!

definitions.text: It's enough to give one the runs!

parts.words: It's enough to give one the runs!
parts.note: the surface suggests something causing diarrhoea; read literally, it is the thing at a cricket ground that shows the runs scored

explanation.surface: A complaint about something that upsets the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'runs' are the points scored, and they are displayed on a board at the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket ground's display board shows the runs each side has made, so it gives spectators the runs.

definitions.meaning: circumstances or situations, a plural noun

explanation.surface: A list of claims and their conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to assert or claim it, and states are also modes or circumstances of being.

clue.text: Haulers in large areas stacked with gold

indicators.note: the areas word is stacked with, i.e. filled by, the gold word, a container signal

parts.note: tracts are large stretches of land
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Lorries carry gold bars piled high across wide territories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stacked with' puts OR inside TRACTS. 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tractors pull farm machinery and trailers, so they are haulers.

clue.text: Note on origin of religion"…without end"

parts.note: te is a sol-fa note, also spelt ti

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter, so this picks the start of the faith word

parts.note: minus means without, as in 'minus his coat'

explanation.surface: A remark about the beginning of a faith, quoting the words 'world without end'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin of' picks R from 'religion'. The quoted 'without end' recalls the liturgy's 'world without end', which makes 'end' look like part of a quotation rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the final point of a line or route, its end.

indicators.note: the letters shiver and jumble about, as if in the cold, giving an anagram

explanation.surface: People living in Siberia must put up with freezing cold on some days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must shiver' rearranges SOMEDAYS. Samoyeds are a Siberian people, and also the white sled dogs bred by them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyeds are a people of northern Siberia, so they are Siberians.

clue.text: Nothing in course of endless searching proves suspect

indicators.note: the zero letter is placed in the searching word, a container signal
endless says the searching word loses its last letter

parts.note: questing is searching or seeking
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A search that turns up nothing shows a suspect was involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts QUESTING to QUESTIN, and 'in' puts O inside it. Here 'suspect' is a verb: to doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: To question something is to doubt it, which is to suspect its truth.

indicators.note: the word reads the same whichever way it blows, from left to right or right to left

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Grass being blown this way and that by the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome: it reads the same in either direction. Marram is the coarse grass planted to bind sand dunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse grass that grows on coastal dunes, so it is a kind of grass.

clue.text: Trendy minister facing Edward's bride-to be

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
to minister to someone is to tend them
Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A fashionable clergyman stands before Edward's fiancee at the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' looks like a clergyman noun, but it is the verb 'tend'.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's intended is the woman he is engaged to marry, his bride-to-be.

clue.text: Disreputable type in low dive's barred

indicators.note: the rogue word is placed in the dive word, a container signal

parts.note: a sty is a filthy place, a low dive
a rip is an old word for a dissolute or worthless person

explanation.surface: A shady character in a seedy bar has been banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barred' means striped, not banned; 'rip' is an old term for a rake or rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something barred is marked with bars or bands, which is what stripy describes.

clue.text: Cheer pilot for righting his craft?

indicators.note: righting means setting the letters to rights, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Cheering on a pilot who is trying to right his aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for righting' rearranges CHEERPILOT. 'his craft' points back to the pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter is an aircraft flown by a pilot, so it is his craft.

parts.note: near-sighted suggests poor eyesight; read literally it is the part of a view seen close up, nearest the viewer

explanation.surface: A myopic person's outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a scene nearest the observer is what is sighted near, as opposed to the background.

clue.text: I agree to hold negative for developing in the dark

indicators.note: the agree word is made to hold the negative word inside it, a container signal

parts.note: to grant is to agree or concede
no is a negative reply

explanation.surface: I agree to keep a photographic negative in the dark until it is developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' puts NO inside GRANT. 'for developing' belongs to the photographic surface, about film needing darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: To be kept in the dark is to be uninformed, which is what ignorant means.

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit

indicators.note: the seen word goes outside the new letter, a container signal

parts.note: met means seen or encountered

explanation.surface: A suit is spotted outside a new window display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' is a lawsuit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a window hinged at the side, so it is a kind of window.

indicators.note: the newspaper word is acquired by the bank word, taken inside it, a container signal

parts.note: a levee is an embankment along a river
rag is slang for a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper bought up by a bank in a takeover deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' means grip or hold, not buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase is a firm hold that gives mechanical advantage, the grip a lever provides.

clue.text: Pure graft I used in cultivation of tree

indicators.note: the letters are worked over as soil is in cultivation, giving an anagram

explanation.surface: A gardener describes the pure graft used in growing a fruit tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in cultivation' rearranges PUREGRAFTI.
explanation.definitionFit: The grapefruit is a citrus tree as well as its fruit.

parts.note: sound suggests healthy or valid; read as a noun it is a narrow channel of sea, and the word also sounds like one meaning direct

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: A sound is a narrow sea channel, which is a strait; the answer also sounds like 'straight', meaning honest or sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow passage of water joining two seas is also called a sound.

clue.text: A dram for one used to hops?

definitions.meaning: someone accustomed to hopping about, one who jigs

explanation.surface: A drink for someone used to beer brewed with hops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hops' looks like the beer ingredient, but here means little jumps: one who jigs.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigger is a small spirits measure, and also, by its form, a person who does jigs or little dancing hops.

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the churchman goes round the state

parts.note: a dean is a senior churchman
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: A clergyman's standing is lowered when he lacks a position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its older sense of 'outside', so DEAN surrounds ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity or standing.

definitions.meaning: made a first appearance, as a show does on its first night

explanation.surface: Something showed up already unfastened.
explanation.definitionFit: A play premieres or appears when it first goes on, and a door that is unfastened is no longer shut.

clue.text: Make up study before Tripos, taking time

annotationWithheld.why: 'Make up study before Tripos, taking time': CON (study) + T would need RIVE, but 'Tripos' gives no such letters; the word is likely an OCR misreading and no source gives the printed clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Make up study before Tripos, taking time

parts.note: to ape someone is to mimic or impersonate them
a bishop is one example of a chessman, a man in chess

explanation.surface: Someone does an impression of a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishop' is a chess piece, and chess pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: Apeman is the term for a primate thought to be intermediate between apes and humans.

clue.text: Suppress southern weed, infusing third of paraquat

indicators.note: the chosen letter is infused into the weed word, a container signal

parts.note: tangle is a kind of seaweed

indicators.note: picks the letter in third position of the weedkiller's name

explanation.surface: A gardener kills southern weeds by dosing them with paraquat weedkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third of' takes R from 'paraquat', and 'infusing' puts it in TANGLE, a seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle something is to stifle or choke it, which is to suppress it.

indicators.note: dropped tells us the line letter is removed from the gossip word

parts.note: a tattler is a gossip or telltale

explanation.surface: A gossip column in a scandal sheet has a line dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rag' looks like a newspaper alongside 'gossip', but it is a scrap of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tatter is a torn scrap of cloth hanging loose, a rag.

parts.note: in order suggests tidy or correct; read literally it means members of a religious order

explanation.surface: Things that are normally arranged correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks and friars in a religious order address one another as brothers.
